task.swarm_objective: Produce a comparative analysis of NVIDIA and AMD's AI-related business performance, supported by financial filings and recent earnings information.
task.agent_directive: Investigate AMD's data-center segment revenue growth (Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs): reported figures, drivers, and cited sources.
constraints: Cite a source for every financial figure you record.
Use the most recently reported fiscal periods.
Focus on the Data Center segment only.
success_criteria: Identify reported Data Center segment revenue for recent quarters
Explain contributions from Instinct and EPYC

tool_arguments.query: AMD Data Center segment revenue Q3 2026 fiscal quarter

events.content: AMD Data Center segment revenue Q3 2026 fiscal quarter

AMD has **not yet reported Q3 2026 results** as of October 17, 2026, so no actual Q3 Data Center segment-revenue figure—or disclosed Q3 split between Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs—is available. 

For Q3 2026, AMD’s guidance is for **total company revenue of approximately $13.0 billion, plus or minus $0.3 billion**; it did not provide Data Center segment guidance in that release. [[1]] 

The latest reported segment result is **Q2 2026 Data Center revenue of $6.7 billion**, up **107% year over year**, driven by strong demand for **AMD EPYC processors** and **AMD Instinct GPUs**. [[1]] 

Management said it expected Data Center sales to **accelerate in the second half of 2026**, citing accelerating EPYC demand, scaling Instinct deployments, and the beginning of the Helios ramp. [[1]]

Sources:
[S1.1] AMD Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results :: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) — https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1295/amd-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results

source_references.title: AMD Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results :: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD)

tool_arguments.query: AMD Q2 2026 Data Center segment revenue Instinct GPUs EPYC contribution

events.content: AMD Q2 2026 Data Center segment revenue Instinct GPUs EPYC contribution

AMD’s Q2 FY2026 Data Center revenue was **$6.718 billion** (reported as $6.7 billion), up **107% year over year** and **16% sequentially**; it represented approximately **58% of AMD’s $11.536 billion** consolidated revenue. [[1]] [[2]] 

AMD did **not disclose separate dollar revenue contributions** for Instinct GPUs versus EPYC CPUs within the segment. [[2]] 

The disclosed drivers were: **EPYC sales rose more than 70% year over year**, supported by record enterprise sell-through, cloud demand, and higher unit shipments and ASPs; **Instinct sales more than doubled year over year**, led by the continued MI350-series ramp and broader adoption among major AI labs and cloud providers. [[2]] 

Thus, both products were material contributors to the $6.7 billion result, but AMD’s public Q2 disclosure does not support a precise Instinct-versus-EPYC revenue split. [[1]] [[2]]

Sources:
[S2.1] AMD Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results :: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) — https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1295/amd-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results
[S2.2] AMD 2Q26 Earnings Call Transcript JOHN: — https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_064d5906a8eb4ebea4947921aef4b9b7/amd/db/841/9237/webcast_transcript/AMD2Q26EarningsCallTranscript.pdf

source_references.title: AMD Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results :: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD)

tool_arguments.query: AMD Q1 2026 Data Center segment revenue Instinct EPYC

events.content: AMD Q1 2026 Data Center segment revenue Instinct EPYC

AMD’s **Q1 2026 Data Center revenue was $5.8 billion**, up **57% year over year**, for the quarter ended March 28, 2026. [[1]] 

AMD attributed the growth to strong demand for **EPYC server processors** and the continued ramp in **Instinct GPU shipments**. [[1]]

Sources:
[S3.1] AMD Reports First Quarter 2026 Financial Results :: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) — https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1284/amd-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results

source_references.title: AMD Reports First Quarter 2026 Financial Results :: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD)

tool_arguments.query: AMD Q2 2026 Ryzen CPU revenue consumer segment

events.content: AMD Q2 2026 Ryzen CPU revenue consumer segment

AMD reported **$3.062 billion of Q2 2026 Client revenue**, its consumer-PC CPU business, up **23% year over year** from $2.499 billion; AMD said the increase was driven primarily by strong demand for **Ryzen processors**. [[1]] [[2]]

Related coverage:
AMD’s **Client and Gaming** segment generated **$14.55 billion** of revenue in FY2025 (year ended December 27, 2025), up **51%** from **$9.65 billion** in FY2024. [[1]] 

Within the segment, **Client** revenue—principally AMD Ryzen desktop and mobile processors—was **$10.64 billion** in FY2025, versus **$7.05 billion** in FY2024. [[1]]

**Gaming** revenue was **$3.91 billion** in FY2025, versus **$2.60 billion** in FY2024; AMD attributed the increase to higher semi-custom revenue, which includes game-console SoCs, and strong demand for Radeon gaming GPUs. [[1]] 

AMD does **not** separately disclose revenue for Ryzen, Radeon, or individual console customers/products, so the reported Gaming figure is the relevant disclosed aggregate for Radeon GPUs and semi-custom console chips. [[1]] 

In Q4 FY2025, Client and Gaming revenue was **$3.94 billion**, comprising **$3.10 billion** of Client revenue and **$843 million** of Gaming revenue. [[2]]

Sources:
[S4.1] AMD Reports Second Quarter 2026 Earnings - AMD Newsroom — https://newsroom.amd.com/news/amd-2q-2026-earnings/
